overview: White develops the bishop to g5 and follows with e3, Nbd2, c3 and Bd3, a set-up with few moves to learn. Black answers ...Be7, ...c5 or ...h6 and ...b6. White aims for e4 or a kingside initiative with the pin on f6, or exchanges Bxf6 to leave Black with doubled pawns.

white_ideas.idea: e3, Nbd2, c3, Bd3 and e4, with the bishop on g5 pinning the f6 knight
Bxf6 to damage Black's structure and play for e4

black_ideas.idea: ...h6 and ...c5 to challenge d4 and kick the bishop

typical_structures.structure: White d4/e3/c3 pyramid against Black ...d5 or ...c5 set-ups

character.notes: Steady development; limited tactics, hard to lose quickly for White.

structure.notes: Centre not committed; White holds d4 and may play e4 later, so flexible.

approach.notes: A set-up (Bg5, e3, Nbd2, c3) played against nearly any Black reply.

level.notes: Anchor-style system: clear plans and little to memorise.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3...c5 4.e3 Qb6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Nf3 e6 3. Bg5 c5 4. e3 Qb6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black attacks b2 and the game gets sharper.

character.reason: Quiet set-up with few ways to lose quickly; Black has some active replies.

structure.reason: Like the London: tense, undecided centre.

approach.reason: A Bg5/e3/Nbd2 set-up played against most defences.

level.reason: Clear plans and little to memorise, like the London.

plans.reason: No plan on the list fits clearly.
